title: Parabolic Long
teaches: The parabolic long as we trade it: Bracco's parabolic burst mirrored, a 3 to 5 day accelerating panic drop that ends on a gap-down climax day, bought only after the turn on the first 5-minute close back over VWAP, the stop a few cents under the climax low, the daily 9 EMA as the target, the one long our 200-day rule allows below the line, and a loss taken at the stop as the cost of being a day early.

facts.quote: any time a successful parabolic short goes down 50-60%+ in a few days, that’s the premise for the long setup.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long comes after a successful parabolic short falls 50-60% or more in a few days.

facts.quote: Entry is opening range highs or the first green 5-minute candle or any range break to the upside if the stock doesn’t rally out of the gate, which they usually do.
facts.claim: Kullamagi's entry: the opening-range high, the first green 5-minute candle or a range break up.

facts.quote: This is by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if you have issues with not obeying your stops.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if stops are not obeyed.

facts.quote: Think of stocks as rubber bands, if they get really stretched short term, they can have powerful snapbacks.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: stocks stretched short term snap back like rubber bands.

facts.quote: These things can bounce 50-100% in a few days.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the bounce can be 50% to 100% in a few days.

facts.quote: Don’t be too early. WAIT for the right setup. Let the amateur shorts get run over, that’s where your edge comes in.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: do not be too early; wait for the right setup.

facts.quote: Most of these are short setups, but sometimes there are also good long setups but they don’t occur as often.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long version is rarer than the short.

facts.quote: Often price will close well off the low in a SC, reflecting the buying by these large interests.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: a selling climax often closes well off its low, as large interests buy.

facts.quote: A wave of buying easily pushes prices up; this is further fueled by short covering.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: the automatic rally is pushed by buying and short covering.

facts.quote: If the ST goes lower than that of the SC, one can anticipate either new lows or prolonged consolidation.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: a test under the climax low means new lows or a long consolidation.

facts.quote: A Reversal Extension is formed when the price pulls away from the moving averages, then snaps back up and is accompanied by heavy volume.
facts.claim: Kell: a Reversal Extension is a snap back from far under the averages on heavy volume.

facts.quote: Stops are placed just below the low of the Reversal Extension bar. Be quick to take profits and raise stops with the first profit target at the retest of the 20 EMA.
facts.claim: Kell: the stop just below the reversal bar's low; be quick to take profits.

facts.quote: Often, trading the daily Reversal Extension is best avoided.
facts.claim: Kell: trading the daily Reversal Extension is often best avoided.

facts.quote: Get aggressive trading individual stocks when you see a Reversal Extension on the index.
facts.claim: Kell: get aggressive in stocks when the index itself prints a Reversal Extension.

facts.quote: That's when price plunges in a straight line drop, day after day, with little or no overlap between price bars.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: a vertical run down plunges day after day with little overlap between bars.

facts.quote: There is minimal overlap from price bar to bar.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: minimal overlap from bar to bar.

facts.quote: Only try this if the event day decline is a large one, say over 30%.
facts.claim: Bulkowski trades a dead-cat bounce only after a one-day drop over 30%.

facts.quote: Price usually gaps downward, closing 15% to 70% lower than the prior day.
facts.claim: Bulkowski's dead-cat bounce starts with a one-day gap down of 15% to 70%.

facts.quote: This is a deadly sin in the market and one of the worst habits an investor can have. Why try to catch a falling dagger?
facts.claim: O'Neil: buying a falling stock is a deadly sin; why catch a falling dagger.

facts.quote: Stocks that decline more than normal are under heavy liquidation by institutional investors and are almost always down for a reason
facts.claim: O'Neil: stocks that fall more than normal are under heavy liquidation for a reason.

facts.quote: I never go against the long-term trend.
facts.claim: Minervini never goes against the long-term trend.

facts.quote: If a stock’s price is in a long-term downtrend, don’t even consider buying it.
facts.claim: Minervini: do not consider buying a stock in a long-term downtrend.

facts.quote: This parabolic burst is a 3-5 day move that marks the final leg of a parabolic move.
facts.claim: Bracco: the parabolic burst is a 3-5 day final leg.

facts.quote: Three straight days of gains. The more consecutive up days, the better the setup.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 1: three straight up days (mirrored: three straight down days).

facts.quote: Two consecutive overnight gap ups. This can include the exhaustion gap on the climax day. Unfilled gaps left behind is a bonus.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 2: two consecutive gap ups, the climax gap may count (mirrored: gap downs).

facts.quote: Two out of three days of range expansion, where the percentage gain is larger than the previous day.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 3: two of three days with a bigger percent move than the day before.

facts.quote: Two days of volume expansion, with each day’s volume higher than the last.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 4: two days of rising volume.

facts.quote: You never know exactly when the climax day will hit, but I won’t short without that gap-up.
facts.claim: Bracco will not short without the climax-day gap (mirrored: the gap down).

facts.quote: The climax gap up typically takes place on day 3 to 5 of the move.
facts.claim: Bracco: the climax gap usually comes on day 3 to 5.

facts.quote: While not every criteria needs to be fully satisfied, the more boxes checked, the stronger the setup.
facts.claim: Bracco: not every box is needed; the more boxes, the stronger.

facts.quote: the climax day almost invariably showing the highest opening volume of the entire run.
facts.claim: Bracco: the climax day almost always has the heaviest opening volume of the run.

facts.quote: I will never take an entry until the stock at least breaks below the intraday VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price).
facts.claim: Bracco never enters the short before the stock breaks under VWAP (mirrored: the long waits for the reclaim).

facts.quote: If the price reclaims the day’s high, I deem my thesis or timing incorrect and exit the trade.

facts.claim: Bracco's target is the daily 9 EMA.

facts.claim: Bracco: a breach of a Bollinger band is usually short-lived and often precedes a snap back.

facts.quote: While this setup is more common in small caps, I prefer mid-to-large cap stocks.
facts.claim: Bracco prefers mid to large caps for the setup.

facts.quote: Being too early to a Parabolic Short is a recipe for disaster.
facts.claim: Bracco: being too early is a recipe for disaster.

facts.quote: Shorting at the day’s highs can be a dangerous trap

facts.quote: You’re lucky to get a couple 5-star candidates a year.
facts.claim: Bracco: a couple of 5-star candidates a year.

facts.claim: Bracco: short-lived trades, not held longer than 1-3 days.

facts.claim: Bracco's Monday Effect: notable capitulations and turns have come on a Monday.

facts.quote: First will be range and volume expansion

facts.quote: Anytime we get a fast move up into 30 it is usually a good time to start paying attention for a mean reversion opportunity.
facts.claim: Bracco: a fast VIX move into 30 is the time to watch for a mean reversion.

facts.claim: Bracco's ideal: a gap down or more weakness before the turn.

facts.quote: Think we really have to keep a 2-3 day outlook until proven otherwise.

facts.claim: E56: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.

facts.claim: The context: a straight-down, accelerating 3 to 5 day burst, a blow-off unwind or a capitulation in a decline.

facts.quote: (4) two days of rising volume; (5) a gap down on the climax day. Two down days can stand in for three if range and ATR expand sharply.
facts.claim: Boxes four and five: two days of rising volume and a gap down on the climax day.

facts.claim: The burst is 3 to 5 sessions; the climax on day 3 to 5.

facts.claim: The target is the daily 9 EMA; the trade is done there.
